summary: ScanStore now marks every folder not listed when it is appended (bit 0x80 of the existing Flags byte) and SetChildren clears the mark. A new public ScanStore.NotListed(int) reads it; Flags() masks the bit off, and Append and AddFlags throw on a caller-supplied 0x80. Scanner.ListRoot appends the root right after the directory check, so a Stop in calls 3 and up of the root's handling leaves a root reading not listed; calls 1 and 2 still leave an empty store. 20 new Core tests, a 5M stopped-at-unlisted-peak memory Fact, and a rule corpus for the widened fitness rule were added. The full suite is 984 passed, 0 failed (964 baseline plus 20 new), with no existing test edited. One gap remains: the app half of criterion 7 is a composed bound, not an app measurement (see deviations).

obligations.how: Rule 1 widened from the single pattern (cast of 0x80 or 128 to EntryFlags) to four: a cast to EntryFlags of a 128 written in decimal, hex or binary with any case, suffix, separators, leading zeros, a 1 << 7 shift, an inner numeric cast or parentheses, and a qualified or global:: type; Enum.ToObject of it; and a mask with the literal on either side of & or &=. The class is closed in tests/bugs/SL-109-NotListedBitRuleCorpus.json, 97 rows, 46 of whose 55 fire rows the first draft let through (shown failing with -Before); every row passes under .NET and under the engine's Python re. mandatory.where: ScanStore.Append sets the mark on every folder, SetChildren alone clears it; tests NotListedTests.CancelAtAnyCallMarksExactlyTheFoldersNotCommitted and AFolderCutPartwayThroughItsBuffersReadsNotListed. The listed-ahead-but-unwritten case cannot occur (no read-ahead reader exists) and is covered by construction, as the design says.
SetChildren clears the mark for any count including 0; NotListedTests.AnEmptyFolderListedBeforeTheStopReadsListed and ACompletedScanLeavesNothingNotListed.

ScanStore.Append and AddFlags throw on 0x80 before any write, AddFlags only ORs, CorrectSizes writes no flags; NotListedTests.ACallerCannotSetTheMark, ACallerCannotSetTheMarkThroughAddFlags, EveryOtherFlagWriteLeavesTheMarkAlone.

Every Kind-byte read is unchanged and a marked folder keeps Kind Folder; NotListedTests.AStoppedStoreRecountsWithNoDifference recounts five stopped stores independently, 0 differences; AMarkedFolderTakesItsChildren... shows CheckParent still accepts children under a marked parent.

ScanStore.Flags() masks the mark and EntryFlags gains no member; NotListedTests.AStoppedStoreClassifiesAsItsMaskedTwin compares a stopped store with a masked replayed twin, and CancelledFolderTests passes unedited (it fails when Flags() shows the mark).
NotListedTests.ACompletedScanLeavesNothingNotListed on two real trees; the 964 existing tests pass with no edit (git diff --diff-filter=M against the merge-base prints nothing).

Half measured, half derived: the mark uses a free bit of the existing Page.Flags byte, and the existing FiveMillionEntriesFitTheMemoryBudget reads 654.6 / 670.6 MiB, identical to the baseline, so no per-entry storage was added. NotListedBudgetTests measured the store at the unlisted peak: retained 637.1 MiB, peak 653.6 MiB, below 800, 60,000 folders marked. The app within 1 GiB is NOT measured with the real app: only the test host's commit (690.0 MiB) was, and the app figure is a composition of that plus the published window's idle 64.9 MiB (about 755 MiB). See deviations.

deviations: PLAN-7 / critique finding M1 (accepted-fixed): the disposition says the design adds a case that records the real App process's private commit at the 5M unlisted-peak shape, driven through FsaWindowHook (stop) and the schema-1 report path, and withdraws the filed-for-later item. The design handed to me still has that item filed for later and a Core-test-host measurement, and the disposition's own assumption (the hook can bring the app to that state without a person and without an impractical tree) does not hold: Core keeps the store private to Scanner.Run, a 5M-entry stopped store in the real window needs a new hook mode feeding a synthetic store (tests/window/FsaWindowHook/**, StartupHook.cs, WindowCases.ps1 parity, gated by Q-114 and lesson #472), or a real tree of about 4.9M entries on disk. I built the earlier version: the Core Fact labelled 'test-host commit', plus a composition with the published window's idle commit (64.9 MiB, measured). Recording it under the app's name would be wrong. The M1 text says that if the assumption is wrong, criterion 7's app half has to be reworded at the brief level; that is not a builder's call.

Rule 1 (fitness.yaml) was widened from one pattern to four and given a corpus (O-015). The design had accepted the narrow pattern; the obligation, decided later, requires the class closed. Rule 2 is left as appended (finding m2 was overridden).

The sweep tree includes a junction (design's list had none) so that 'no file or link reads NotListed' is exercised on a stopped store; completed-scan coverage of a junction and a long path is a second tree, as designed.

The memory Fact's generator caps listings at 12 deep and lists folders empty at the cap and once the entries-before-W budget is spent, so the stack drains and W is listed last; the shape is 4.34M files and 0.54M folders (U-001: 4.5M and 0.5M) with 300,000 names sharing 100,000 IDs. It also records GC.GetGCMemoryInfo().TotalCommittedBytes and collects twice before the before-build reading, which finding m6 asked for and the person waived to SC-369; both are output-only.

The store tests use a few more files than the design listed: O-002 and O-004 each got their own Fact (AFolderCutPartwayThroughItsBuffersReadsNotListed, ARootNotYetKnownToBeAFolderLeavesNoRootToMark) so each obligation has a command that runs only its shape.
not_built: No App view of NotListed (a 'not read yet' note): the design builds only the store's read (D1).
No SubtreeUnfinished marker, as designed (U-204 impossible as stated).
The real App's commit at a stopped 5M-entry store: see deviations and follow_ups.

The RootUnreadable one-entry result (a root whose first List call fails with a non-cancel error and keeps nothing) has no Fact: finding m7 was waived to SC-370. The behaviour is in the code and stated in the design record.
The block-wise-writer invariant (finding m4) is stated in SetChildren's doc comment and docs/design/SL-109-not-listed.md only; the waiver carried any further work to SC-368.
Cancel on a stalled share and Network=SMB-LOOPBACK were not re-run (a person's run; the TEST-NET-1 guard is red at baseline, Q-259). The record says so and makes no stop-safety claim on shares.
No read-ahead reader and no test for 'listed ahead but not yet written': no code path produces the shape (material: false in the design).
follow_ups: Measure the published WPF app's own commit with a stopped 5M-entry store at its unlisted peak: needs a FsaWindowHook mode that feeds a synthetic store to the real window (gated by Q-114's WindowMutants run). Until then criterion 7's app half is a composed bound of about 755 MiB, or the brief's wording has to change.
A 'not read yet' view that consumes ScanStore.NotListed in the stopped or paused results (U-182's last condition): unlisted folders still show '0 bytes' with no note.
If a view needs it, a 'subtree not finished' marker derived from NotListed plus the depth-first order (not done here; needs Kind masking if stored).
Person-run network pass (Network=SMB-LOOPBACK, Cancel on a stalled share) is stale again because Scanner.cs changed.
The next flag needs a new byte column or Kind bits: bit 0x80 of Flags is now the last free one.
Findings m4, m6 and m7 are on the backlog as SC-368, SC-369 and SC-370.

architecture.replace: Folders keep firstChild/childCount/filesBelow. A folder is appended marked not listed and only registering its children (SetChildren, even with none) clears the mark, so a stopped store tells a folder it never listed from one it listed and found empty (ScanStore.NotListed); the mark lives in bit 0x80 of the existing flags byte, which Flags() never returns.
